78	
79	- `session <sid>: setup complete`, Setup's last action;
80	- `Task <N>: report <status> <one line>`, after an implementer's report;
81	- `Task <N>: review <approved|blocking> <reviewer id> <one line>`, after a task review or scoped re-review;
82	- `Task <N>: codex gate round <R> <approved|blocking> <one line>`, after each per-task Codex gate round.
83	
84	## Rules for every step
85	
86	These hold in every step file. Where a step file and this section differ, this section governs.
87	
88	- Tasks with a `Task <N>: complete` line are DONE — do not re-dispatch them. Conversation memory does not survive compaction. After compaction, trust the ledger and `git log` over your own recollection.
89	- Dispatch implementer, task-reviewer, fix-round, re-review and final-reviewer subagents with `run_in_background: false`. Your next step always depends on the result, and a foreground call keeps your turn open, which is what an editor such as Zed shows as the session working. A background dispatch ends the turn while the subagent runs, and the editor shows the session idle.
90	- Run a covering command expected to finish within 10 minutes in the foreground, with an explicit timeout of at least its expected runtime and at most 600000 ms. A command that may run past 10 minutes is a tracked job; [task-loop.md](task-loop.md), "Waiting on subagents and long commands", gives its commands and watch budget.
91	- One implementer at a time in this session: parallel work is other sessions' (one controller per task branch); never dispatch two implementers at once here.
92	- Never fix findings yourself in the controller session — your context stays clean for coordination, and controller fixes skip review. The one exception is the de-minimis fix in [fix-loop.md](fix-loop.md).
93	- The task reviewer's blocking findings and the per-task Codex gate's blocking findings form one loop with ONE shared cap of **five rounds per task**: the gate does not run a count of its own.
94	- When round 5's re-review — or a per-task Codex gate at the spent cap — still leaves blocking findings open, stop dispatching and surface the task as BLOCKED, as [fix-loop.md](fix-loop.md) describes under the breaker.
95	
96	## Model Selection
97	
98	Match the model to the task's difficulty rather than defaulting. Two rules are
99	defaults you will get wrong by omission, so they stay here: **always specify
100	the model explicitly when dispatching a subagent** — an omitted model inherits
101	your session's, usually the most capable and most expensive — and **a mid-tier
102	model is the floor for reviewers and for implementers working from prose
103	descriptions**, whatever the schedule pressure. The cheapest tier is for
104	transcription, where the task's own text carries the complete code to write,
105	and for single-file mechanical fixes. The per-role guidance, the complexity
106	signals, and the fix-loop escalation rule are in
107	[model-selection.md](model-selection.md).
108	
109	## The waiting board
110	
111	Before you ask your human partner a question, hand back BLOCKED, meet an
112	empty frontier (`held` or `blocked`), or stop on a merge conflict, post what
113	you wait on: `scripts/sdd-state wait PLAN_FILE --session <sid> --kind
114	<question|tasks|merge|gate|handoff> [--task N] --note "<one line>"`, and put
115	the session lines of `scripts/sdd-state board PLAN_FILE` in what you write.
116	When you resume, clear it: `scripts/sdd-state wait PLAN_FILE --session <sid> --clear`.
117	The board is how your human partner finds the session that needs them among
118	several; a session that holds a claim and posts nothing shows as quiet
119	after half an hour, which is where they look for a permission prompt.
120	
121	## Risk Tiers (per-task Codex gate applicability)
122	
123	Tiers are `low`, `standard`, `high`, declared per task in the plan. A task
124	skips the per-task Codex gate only when all three hold: declared low, the
125	plan's own Codex gate actually reviewed the plan, and no escalation trigger
126	fired at any point during execution. That skip is recorded durably. An
127	unreviewed low tier — plan gate skipped, degraded, or outcome unknown —
128	executes as standard, and a task demoted that way runs the full train and
129	records NO tier-skip event. The Claude task reviewer and the final
130	whole-branch train never tier off. When any task did skip, write
131	`tier-skips.md` in this plan's workspace; Final Review hands its path to the
132	final reviewer and the final Codex gate. The escalation triggers, the
133	fallback rules, and the exact ledger line shape are in
134	[risk-tiers.md](risk-tiers.md) — read it before dispatching any task declared
135	low.
136	
137	## Common Rationalizations
138	
139	The excuses that show up mid-run and what is actually true:
140	[common-rationalizations.md](common-rationalizations.md). Read it the moment you
141	catch yourself justifying a shortcut.
142	
143	## Example Workflow
144	
145	A complete worked run, dispatch through finish:
146	[example-workflow.md](example-workflow.md).
147

1	## Final Review
2	
3	Part of [SKILL.md](SKILL.md); the rules there hold in this step.
4	
5	The final train is claimed. When `next` says `complete`, run
6	`scripts/sdd-state claim PLAN_FILE final --session <sid>`: `claimed` means
7	this session runs the final review, the final gate and Finish; `blocked`
8	names tasks still open (claims without completion lines elsewhere: wait or
9	ask); `held` with your own session id (`own=1`, a resume after compaction)
10	means this session already holds the train: continue as its holder; `held`
11	names the session that holds it, or `lease=<sid> plan=<ws>`
12	when a sibling plan's final holds the branch: post a `tasks` record naming
13	the holder, print the board, and hand back. The holder checks the
14	integration branch out in its own worktree (`git switch <integration>`), the
15	one time a session does so, and runs the review package, the final
16	reviewer, the fix wave and the final Codex gate on it; its fix commits land
17	on the integration branch directly, which the lease makes safe.
18	
19	Once you hold the train and have checked the integration branch out, the
20	final whole-branch review gets a package too: run
21	`scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE MERGE_BASE HEAD` (MERGE_BASE = the commit the
22	branch started from, e.g. `git merge-base main HEAD`) — take the path from the
23	`wrote <path>: ...` line and include it in the final review dispatch, so the
24	final reviewer reads one file instead of re-deriving the branch diff with git
25	commands. Dispatch
26	on the most capable available model (see Model Selection), using
27	hyperpowers:requesting-code-review's
28	[code-reviewer.md](../requesting-code-review/code-reviewer.md). Point it at
29	the ledger's deferred-minor lines — and at `tier-skips.md`, if any task
30	skipped its per-task gate — so it can triage which must be fixed before
31	merge.
32	
33	If the final whole-branch review returns findings, dispatch ONE fix subagent
34	with the complete findings list — not one fixer per finding. Compose the
35	dispatch from [fix-subagent-prompt.md](fix-subagent-prompt.md).
36	Per-finding fixers each rebuild context and re-run suites; a real
37	session's final-review fix wave cost more than all its tasks combined.
38	Then run exactly one scoped re-review of the fix wave
39	(`scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE FIX_BASE HEAD` over the fix range,
40	[re-review-prompt.md](re-review-prompt.md) using its Final-wave usage note).
41	There is no second fix wave: anything the re-review leaves open — and any
42	finding that conflicts with the plan's text — goes to your human partner
43	with the evidence, as BLOCKED, when finishing-a-development-branch presents
44	the options.
45	
46	**Dispatch the decision extractor.** When the ledger has a `Decisions listing:`
47	line (and otherwise nothing), once the fix wave and its re-review are
48	clean (or the final review returned no findings), take a scratch directory
49	from `../requesting-code-review/scripts/codex-review-dir`, regenerate the
50	full-branch package (`scripts/review-package PLAN_FILE MERGE_BASE HEAD`, so a
51	fix wave's commits are in it) and copy it and `<workspace>/progress.md` into
52	it, and dispatch the
53	extractor in the background, composed from
54	`../finishing-a-development-branch/decision-notes-prompt.md` with those two
55	copies, the plan, the spec, the `Decisions listing:` from the ledger, the
56	index (`decisions/README.md` beside the spec's directory) when it exists, and
57	`<dir>/decision-notes.md` as its output path. Record it in the ledger:
58	`Decision extractor: <task id> -> <dir>/decision-notes.md`. The dispatch is
59	complete only when that line is in the ledger: write it before any other tool
60	call, because after a compaction it is the only record of the task id and the
61	notes path, and without it a resumed controller can neither collect nor stop
62	the extractor. The extractor reads nothing inside the workspace, so Finish may
63	delete the workspace while it runs;
64	finishing-a-development-branch collects it after the full suite and never
65	waits for it, and neither do you. On a harness with no tracked background
66	subagent, skip the dispatch and note it in the ledger. If a Codex final-gate
67	fix changes code after the dispatch: stop the extractor (TaskStop); when the
68	fix altered one of the spec's decisions, settle that first (show your human
69	partner the change you would write into the `## Decisions` item, write and
70	commit it on the branch with their approval; without it the item stands and
71	the change is raised again at the menu); re-run the dry run and replace the
72	ledger's `Decisions listing:`; regenerate the full-branch package and copy
73	it, with the current `<workspace>/progress.md`, into the scratch directory,
74	replacing the earlier copies; compose the replacement dispatch from those
75	copies; then dispatch the extractor again and replace the
76	`Decision extractor:` line.
77	
78	**Codex Review Gate — final whole-branch (Claude Code only).** After the final code-reviewer
79	subagent and its fix wave, and before hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch,
80	run the gate using the final whole-branch code recipe with `--base <branch
81	merge-base, e.g. git merge-base main HEAD>`. Provide the branch
82	review-package path, plan or requirements path, the Minor findings ledger if
83	present, and the tier-skip summary if any task skipped. The final dossier passes the plan's `**Spec:**` file as a `--doc` input beside the plan, and carries the tier-skip summary among its `--adjudications`. Resolve blocking
84	findings with one fix subagent carrying the complete list, per this
85	section's existing guidance, before finishing. After any Codex-triggered
86	final-review fix, re-run the final code-reviewer before re-running the final
87	Codex gate.
88	
89	Unlike the per-task gate, the final gate keeps a ceiling of its own: the
90	gate's convergence stop-rule and per-gate backstop bound this loop (code
91	gates use a code-gate backstop of 3 rounds). If the backstop is hit with
92	unresolved blocking findings, surface them to your human partner rather than
93	looping.
94	
95	## Finish
96	
97	When the final whole-branch review is clean and its fixes are merged:
98	
99	1. **Read your session line** from the ledger (its `mode`), and copy the
100	   ledger's `Decisions listing:` and `Decision extractor:` lines (or its
101	   skip reason) into the hand-off message you are about to send: the next
102	   step removes the ledger from the working tree, and
103	   hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch takes the mode, the plan, the
104	   spec and the extractor's task id and output path as its input.
105	2. **Finish the workspace** with `scripts/sdd-state finish PLAN_FILE --session <sid>`:
106	   it refuses with `open-claims` while any claimed task lacks a completion line
107	   (that is a plan not finished, not a reason for `--force`), and with
108	   `busy` (exit 3) when another session is writing the workspace or a copy
109	   from an interrupted removal sits beside it (report the stderr line, wait
110	   for the other session or ask your human partner about the copy, then run
111	   `finish` again); it also refuses with `live-jobs` while a tracked job it
112	   names is still live (run `tracked-job wait` on it, or `tracked-job stop`
113	   when the job is no longer wanted, then run `finish` again). `not-holder`
114	   or `no-final-claim` (exit 11): this session does not hold the final
115	   train; stop and hand back. Otherwise it
116	   removes the plan's directory, commits the removal to the state branch,
117	   and prints `last=<sha>`, the commit that still holds the dossier,
118	   `push=<remote>/<branch>` and `receipt=<path>`, the durable copy of the
119	   ledger, the guard's log and the job records; record the receipt path in
120	   your closing message. A line reading `receipt=none staging=<path>` means
121	   the record exists only under that staging path: name the path to your
122	   human partner in the closing message. A space in either path prints as
123	   `%20`, so decode it before you name the path. On the plain backend it
124	   prints `backend=plain` instead of `last=` and `push=`, and there is
125	   nothing to push. `none` means there was no workspace to remove, and
126	   `error` (exit 2) that the removal or its commit failed: any status other
127	   than `finished` stops Finish until the command
128	   succeeds; show its stderr line.
129	3. **Verify deletion** with `test ! -d "<workspace>"` to confirm it is gone.
130	   The push command is `git -C <checkout> push <remote> <branch>`, the
131	   checkout being the parent of the `plans/` directory `sdd-dir` printed;
132	   run it only if your human partner asks.
133	4. **Keep the lease through the branch action.** `finish` leaves the branch
134	   lease in place; hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch marks the
135	   branch closing before a merge and releases the lease after whichever
136	   option your human partner chose. Hand it the plan path and your session
137	   id for that. When the final ends with a hand-back instead, detach your
138	   worktree first (`git switch --detach`) and then release the lease
139	   yourself, as the last action:
140	   `scripts/sdd-state lease PLAN_FILE --release --session <sid>`.
141	
142	A clean finish that leaves the workspace behind is an INCOMPLETE finish —
143	"keeping it for reference" is not an option; the repo's commits are the
144	durable record. Sibling directories belong to other plans; leave them
145	alone. `scripts/sdd-state prune --repo <dir>` is the only other remover, and it
146	runs only when asked.
147	
148	Use hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch, passing the mode from your
149	session line. Hand it the plan and the spec, and the extractor's task id
150	and output path when one was dispatched; when the dispatch was skipped,
151	hand over the ledger's reason instead and say so, and finishing compiles
152	without notes; when the plan has no spec, say that, and finishing runs its
153	test-only path. A decision a Codex-gate fix altered was settled in Final
154	Review before the re-dispatch.
155

steps.message:
### Strengths
- **The code matches the plan exactly.** `src/textstats.js` is the plan's Step 3 blocks for all four tasks, joined in order. Each task only appended its function and widened the export line, so no earlier code was rewritten. `tokenize` is the only definition of a word, and `wordCount`, `sentenceCount`, `topWords` and `readingTimeMinutes` (through `wordCount`) all use it. The stop-word list has the 36 entries the plan specifies. The tie-break uses `<` and `>`, not `localeCompare`.
- **Commit rules were followed.** There are four `feat:` commits, one per task, and each holds exactly its test file plus `src/textstats.js`.
- **The brief tests were kept verbatim.** I checked this by script: the brief's test code is an exact prefix of `test/wordCount.test.js`, `test/sentenceCount.test.js` and `test/topWords.test.js`. The one change is noted below.
- **The added tests are good, and every behaviour the plan's prose describes now has a test.** They cover joiners, dashes, slashes and underscores, decimals and domains, non-Latin scripts, all 11 abbreviations plus case folding, closing quotes and brackets, the full set of bad `wpm` values (`-0`, `true`, `[200]` and so on), fractional `wpm`, text checked before rate, and mutation safety.
- **Expected values were checked independently.** The Task 1 passage really is 64 words by `wc -w` (I confirmed this). The Task 2 passage has 8 sentences by my own count.
- **The Task 3 passage test avoided a trap in the plan.** The plan's comment lists `storm x1` beside the top four, which suggests `storm` is fifth. But `climbed`, `hand`, `lit`, `old`, `older` and `shook` also appear once and sort before `storm`. The implementer pinned only the first four entries and looked up `storm` by name, so the test is correct.
- **Tests pass.** `npm test` at the head gives 75 passed, 0 failed (I ran it).

### Issues

#### Critical (Must Fix)
None.

#### Important (Should Fix)
None.

#### Minor (Nice to Have)
1. **One verbatim brief line was edited.** At `test/readingTimeMinutes.test.js:3` the import became `{ readingTimeMinutes, wordCount }` instead of the brief's `{ readingTimeMinutes }`. The added tests at lines 64-68 and 106-120 need it. It is harmless and justified, but strictly it breaks the "keep verbatim" decision, so please confirm it was intended.
2. **The Task 3 order test was not proven red (deferred from the task review).** `test/topWords.test.js:127-129` asserts only `TypeError`. Before Task 3 existed, calling `topWords` already threw `TypeError: topWords is not a function`, so the test's first failure proved nothing. It does catch the real mistake today: checking `n` first would throw `RangeError` and fail the test. Optional fix: also assert that the message starts with `topWords:`, as the matching readingTimeMinutes test at `test/readingTimeMinutes.test.js:96-104` does. Not a blocker.
3. **The Task 3 single-test reference table (deferred).** It is required by the plan and the same in all four files. No action needed.

### Recommendations
- **Two plan-text problems, for future plans:**
  - Task 3's PASSAGE comment wrongly suggests `storm` is fifth in the ranking.
  - Task 4's prose describes a "multi-paragraph test" of 270 words that its own test block does not contain. The implementer correctly added it at `test/readingTimeMinutes.test.js:60-68`.
- **A known limit, not a defect.** An abbreviation from the list that ends a sentence (for example "Main St. It is…") will undercount sentences. The plan accepts this trade-off on purpose.

### Assessment

**Ready to merge?** Yes

**Reasoning:** The code is the plan's specified code, every behaviour in the plan's prose has a correct, independently checked test, and all 75 tests pass. Neither deferred Task 3 finding needs fixing before merge. I reviewed the whole branch in one pass, without subagents, and changed nothing in the checkout.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/johnss51/.cache/hyperpowers/compaction-reread-notice/arms/slice/skills/finishing-a-development-branch

# Finishing a Development Branch

## Overview

**Core principle:** Record decisions and verify tests → Detect environment → Present options → Execute choice → Clean up.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."

**REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use hyperpowers:communication for the test-failure report and the PR description. The option menus below are presented exactly as written.

## Step 1: Record Decisions and Verify Tests

A branch that implements a spec leaves one record per decision in the
`decisions/` directory beside the spec's directory, compiled by
`scripts/decisions-compile` in this skill's directory from the spec's
`## Decisions` list, with the plan removed in the same commit. The records
ride the branch before any merge or push, so they are staged here and
committed in Step 4 once your human partner has seen them. Work with no spec
has no records: for it, this step is the test run alone.

1. **Find the plan and the spec.** Start from the repository root:

   ```bash
   cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
   ```

   Run this step and Step 4 from the repository root; every path below is
   repository-relative, as the compiler and the pathspec file expect. Then
   fix the fork point, in every case, because the steps below diff and
   search from it (the base branch is whatever this work forked from,
   usually named in the plan, the conversation, or the branch's upstream;
   when it is not already known, ask now, before anything below runs: "This
   branch split from <your best guess> - is that correct?"):

   ```bash
   MERGE_BASE=$(git merge-base <base-branch> HEAD)
   ```

   The subagent-driven-development hand-off names both. Otherwise read the
   branch's history, not its tree, so a plan an earlier records commit
   removed is still found:

   ```bash
   git log --diff-filter=A --name-only --format= "$MERGE_BASE"..HEAD -- '*/plans/*.md'
   ```

   Exactly one plan is the plan; read its `**Spec:**` header from the commit
   that added it (`git show <sha>:<path>`). More than one: ask your human
   partner which applies. A plan without a Spec header, or with `none`: ask
   the same way. No plan: when the branch's history added or changed a spec
   (`git log --diff-filter=AM --name-only --format= "$MERGE_BASE"..HEAD -- '*/specs/*.md'`),
   ask whether records are wanted for it, and if so there is a spec and no
   plan; when it did neither, the work is bounded: there is no spec, skip
   the extractor and go to the test run in item 3.
2. **Take a scratch directory and dry-run the compiler.** The directory
   comes from `../requesting-code-review/scripts/codex-review-dir` (one per
   finish; the extractor's output and the pathspec file `records.paths` live
   in it, whether or not an extractor is dispatched). Then
   `bash <this skill's directory>/scripts/decisions-compile <spec> --dry-run`,
   with `--plan <plan>` added when a plan was found.
   Exit 2 for a missing decisions list is the legacy-spec case: draft the
   `## Decisions` list from the spec's own text, one item per decision it
   states, show it to your human partner, and write it into the spec once
   they approve it, and commit that edit on the branch before going on (a
   docs commit of the spec alone; the compiler requires a committed spec,
   and a skip restores the spec from HEAD). Any other exit 2 names what to fix first (a spec that is
   not committed, a plan that is not a tracked and clean markdown file under
   `plans/` whose Spec header names this spec, or a `Supersedes:` problem):
   resolve it with them before going on. Keep the numbered listing for the
   extractor.
3. **Dispatch the extractor, then run the suite.** Skip the dispatch when the
   branch has no spec, when the hand-off already names an extractor (a task
   id and an output path), when the branch already carries this spec's
   records commit (`git log "$MERGE_BASE"..HEAD --fixed-strings --grep="docs: record decisions for <spec filename without -design.md>"`,
   the subject Step 4's commit uses for this spec), or
   when your harness has no tracked background subagent (then say so when
   you hand back). Otherwise compose the dispatch from
   [decision-notes-prompt.md](decision-notes-prompt.md) with the merge-base
   diff and `<dir>/decision-notes.md` as its output path, and start it in
   the background. Then run the project's full test suite (`npm test` /
   `cargo test` / `pytest` / `go test ./...`) and wait for its result in
   this turn:
   - A suite expected to finish within 10 minutes runs in the foreground,
     with an explicit timeout of at least its expected runtime and at most
     600000 ms.
   - A suite that may run longer starts through your harness's tracked
     background option (`run_in_background` on Claude Code, with a timeout
     above its expected runtime), never with a trailing `&` or `nohup`, as
     `<suite> > <dir>/suite.log 2>&1; echo $? > <dir>/suite.exit`. `<dir>`
     is the scratch directory from item 2; when item 2 was skipped, take
     one the same way now. Then wait in the foreground with repeated
     `bash <this skill's directory>/scripts/wait-exit <dir>/suite.exit --max-ms 540000`
     calls, each with a 600000 ms tool timeout: `running` means call it
     again; `exited code=0` is a green suite; any other code is a failing
     suite, read from `<dir>/suite.log`. A launch whose timeout passes with
     no exit file is a failing suite too.

   Ending the turn while the suite runs leaves an editor such as Zed
   showing the session idle, and there the result goes unreported until
   your human partner types.
4. **If tests fail**, stop a still-running extractor (TaskStop), report the
   failures and stop — the menu comes after a green suite. Nothing is
   compiled; the plan stays.

   ```
   Tests failing (<N> failures). Must fix before completing:

   [Show failures]
   ```

5. **If tests pass** and the branch has a spec, collect the extractor without
   waiting: finished, its file is the `--notes`; unfinished, stop it
   (TaskStop), compile without notes, and say so when you hand back. The spec
   must be clean before the compile (no uncommitted edits; commit or stash
   them), because a skip restores it from HEAD. A spec that already carries
   an Outcome line is a spec another plan finished first; the compiler
   recompiles it, adding this plan to the Outcome line and its notes as
   their own paragraph. It refuses three cases, each with exit 2 and nothing
   written: this plan has the file name of a plan the spec already records;
   notes from a finish without a plan would replace notes plans wrote; or
   this plan's notes would replace notes a finish without a plan wrote. Show
   the stderr line and stop. When the hand-off names a
   dossier (SDD), first record where the board and the lease find the plan,
   because the compile removes the plan file and can empty its directory,
   and Step 6 can remove this worktree. `PLAN_REPO` is the main checkout of
   the plan's repository: it survives Step 6, and it is the plan repository
   even when the code lives in another one. `PLAN_REL` is the plan's path
   inside that repository. Both are asked from the plan's nearest existing
   directory, so a finish restarted after an earlier records commit records
   the same values (an SDD branch with no spec runs no compile and records
   them the same way before Step 4). `<plan>` in the lease commands below is
   `"$PLAN_REPO/$PLAN_REL"`.

   ```bash
   dir=$(dirname <plan>); rest=$(basename <plan>)
   while [ ! -d "$dir" ]; do rest="$(basename "$dir")/$rest"; dir=$(dirname "$dir"); done
   PLAN_REPO=$(git -C "$dir" worktree list --porcelain | sed -n '1s/^worktree //p')
   PLAN_REL=$(git -C "$dir" rev-parse --show-prefix)$rest
   ```

   Then run
   `bash <this skill's directory>/scripts/decisions-compile <spec> --plan <plan> --notes <file> --paths-file <dir>/records.paths`,
   omitting `--plan` when the branch has no plan and `--notes` when there is
   no notes file. A `notes ignored:` line on its stderr is repeated verbatim
   when you hand back. On exit 2, resolve the named problem and re-run; on
   exit 3, report the git failure and re-run once it is cleared. Nothing is
   committed here; the staged set waits for Step 4. Continue to Step 2.

## Step 2: Detect Environment

```bash
GIT_DIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
GIT_COMMON=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
# Capture now, while still inside the workspace — Step 5 changes directory
# before cleanup (Step 6) needs this value
WORKTREE_PATH=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
```

The skill that called you may pass the session's mode (`current-branch`,
`new-branch`, or `worktree`): subagent-driven-development reads it from the
ledger's `session` line before the workspace is finished, executing-plans
carries it from the branch question. A passed `new-branch` or `worktree`
changes nothing here: the environment rows below govern them as they do
today. A passed `current-branch` selects one of the two `current-branch`
rows and the environment rows do not apply to it; on the default branch it
also skips Step 3 and Step 6, on any other branch Step 3 and Step 6 run as
for the standard menu.
The repository's default branch is the branch `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`
points at when that ref exists; otherwise whichever one of `main` and
`master` exists as a local branch; when both exist, the one
`init.defaultBranch` names, and when it names neither, ask your human
partner which is the default before choosing a row; when neither exists,
the `init.defaultBranch` value, otherwise `master`:

```bash
CURRENT_BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)
DEFAULT_BRANCH=$(git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null | sed 's|^origin/||')
if [ -z "$DEFAULT_BRANCH" ]; then
  HAVE_MAIN=$(git show-ref --verify -q refs/heads/main && echo yes) || true
  HAVE_MASTER=$(git show-ref --verify -q refs/heads/master && echo yes) || true
  CONFIGURED=$(git config --get init.defaultBranch) || true
  if [ "$HAVE_MAIN" = yes ] && [ "$HAVE_MASTER" = yes ]; then
    case "$CONFIGURED" in main|master) DEFAULT_BRANCH=$CONFIGURED ;; *) DEFAULT_BRANCH="" ;; esac
  elif [ "$HAVE_MAIN" = yes ]; then DEFAULT_BRANCH=main
  elif [ "$HAVE_MASTER" = yes ]; then DEFAULT_BRANCH=master
  else DEFAULT_BRANCH=${CONFIGURED:-master}
  fi
fi
# An empty DEFAULT_BRANCH here means both branches exist and the config
# names neither: ask before choosing a row.
```

This determines which menu to show and how cleanup works:

| State | Menu | Cleanup |
|-------|------|---------|
| `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON` (normal repo) | Standard 3 options | No worktree to clean up |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, named branch | Standard 3 options | Provenance-based (see Step 6) |
| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, detached HEAD | Reduced 2 options (no merge) | Externally managed — leave in place |
| mode `current-branch` passed, `$CURRENT_BRANCH` is `$DEFAULT_BRANCH` | Reduced 2 options (push, keep) | None: no branch and no worktree were created |
| mode `current-branch` passed, any other branch | Standard 3 options | Option 1 deletes the merged branch as usual; no worktree to remove |
| `$DEFAULT_BRANCH` is empty (both `main` and `master` exist, `init.defaultBranch` names neither) | Ask your human partner which is the default, then read this table again | Decided by the row their answer selects |

## Step 3: Determine Base Branch

Skip this step when mode `current-branch` was passed and `$CURRENT_BRANCH`
is `$DEFAULT_BRANCH`: there is no merge and no base to confirm. A
`current-branch` session on any other branch needs its base like any
feature branch.

The base branch is the one Step 1 confirmed: whatever this work forked
from, usually named in the plan, the conversation, or the branch's
upstream. When Step 1 had no spec and did not ask, confirm it here the same
way (ask "This branch split from <your best guess> - is that correct?").
Confirm before merging: merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo.

## Step 4: Present Options

**When Step 1 staged records,** the message that presents the options, from
the repository root as in Step 1, opens
with the complete staged diff over the pathspec file's paths (`git diff` has
no pathspec-file option, so the NUL-delimited file is read into an array; a
path with a space survives, and the variable makes the entries literal, as
the compiler's own git calls are, so a bracket or star in a spec name
matches only itself):

```bash
PATHS_FILE=<dir>/records.paths
paths=(); while IFS= read -r -d '' p; do paths+=("$p"); done < "$PATHS_FILE"
GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1 git diff --cached -- "${paths[@]}"
```

The message carries that command's output itself, verbatim; a summary, a
list of paths or a pointer to a tool result is not the diff, and no option is
accepted until the diff has been shown. Then the extractor's proposals from
its notes file, each with the question
it needs: an undocumented decision (add it to the spec's `## Decisions`
list, or dismiss it); a proposed supersession (add a
`Supersedes: <record path>` line to the item that reverses that record, or
dismiss it); then one line offering to skip the records for this branch; and
only then the menu text exactly as written below. Your human partner answers
once. An answer that names an option but leaves any proposal without a
disposition is incomplete: ask for the missing dispositions and wait; nothing
is written or committed until every proposal has one. A skip is settled
before any accepted proposal is written: an answer that both accepts a
proposal and skips is incomplete, so ask which they mean. Unless they chose
the skip, before executing their option: write each accepted proposal into the spec (an accepted undocumented
decision is appended after the list's last item, never inserted, so the
numbers the notes use stay with their records; an accepted supersession is a
`Supersedes:` line on the item it belongs to),
then re-run the compiler with the same arguments (it stages the spec,
carrying the proposal and the Outcome line, with the records and the index),
and because the staged set
changed, show the new complete staged diff and ask only for its approval,
not the dispositions again; record a dismissal in the hand-back in their
words. An approval leads to the one records commit below, which takes the
spec too through the pathspec file; a withheld approval commits nothing,
keeps the staged set and the spec edit in place, and asks what to change (the
skip was settled before any proposal was written, so `--undo` is not this
path's tool). If they change their mind to a skip at that point, first take
the accepted proposal back out of the spec and stage the spec again
(`GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1 git add -- <spec>`), so `--undo` sees no later edit; record the proposal's
text in the hand-back, so their words are not lost; then follow the skip
path. A skip ends the records for this branch:
run `bash <this skill's directory>/scripts/decisions-compile --undo <spec> --plan <plan>` (without `--plan` when there
is none), record it in their words, make no commit, and run the option they
chose. Otherwise commit:

```bash
GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1 git commit --pathspec-from-file=<dir>/records.paths --pathspec-file-nul -m "docs: record decisions for <spec filename without -design.md>"
```

The message is that one line and nothing else: no second `-m`, no trailer, no
attribution or `Co-Authored-By` line, whatever the harness suggests. An empty
pathspec file means there is nothing to commit (the branch already carries
its records): skip the commit and run the chosen option.

The option runs only after that commit succeeds. If it fails (a hook, an
index conflict, anything), show the failure, stop, and run the same commit
again once the cause is cleared; nothing is merged or pushed while the
records and the plan's deletion are merely staged.

Then run the option they chose. A branch with no records shows the menu as it
always did.

**Plans that share the integration branch.** When the hand-off names a
dossier (SDD), run `bash <this skill's directory>/../subagent-driven-development/scripts/sdd-state board --repo "$PLAN_REPO"`:
`PLAN_REPO` is the main checkout of the plan file's repository, recorded in
Step 1 before the compile, where the dossier lives, which is not the code
repository when the plan lives elsewhere. When it lists
another open plan whose `integration=` is this branch, the merge option is
withheld. The withheld-merge line replaces option 1 only in a menu that
offers a merge: present the three-option menu with option 1 replaced by the
line `1. (merge withheld: plan <ws> is still open on this branch)` and
accept only options 2 and 3. The two-option menus (mode `current-branch` on
the default branch, and a detached HEAD) have no merge option and are shown
unchanged. In every menu, say which plan is open, and a pull request's
description states that another plan is still open on the branch.

**Normal repo and named-branch worktree — present exactly these 3 options:**

```
Implementation complete. What would you like to do?

1. Merge back to <base-branch> locally
2. Push and create a Pull Request
3. Keep the branch as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

**Mode `current-branch` on the default branch — present exactly these 2 options:**

```
Implementation complete on <branch>. What would you like to do?

1. Push <branch>
2. Keep as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

**Detached HEAD — present exactly these 2 options:**

```
Implementation complete. You're on a detached HEAD (externally managed workspace).

1. Push as new branch and create a Pull Request
2. Keep as-is (I'll handle it later)

Which option?
```

Present the menu exactly as written — concise, with every option coming
from the list above. Discarding the work happens only in response to your
human partner explicitly asking for it (see "If your human partner asks to
discard the work" below). Wait for their answer; the integration decision
is theirs.

## Step 5: Execute Choice

### Mode current-branch on the default branch

The two-option menu above maps to: option 1 pushes exactly this branch,
`git push <remote> <branch>:<branch>` (add `-u` when the branch has no
upstream yet), where `<remote>` is the first of `git config
branch.<branch>.pushRemote`, `git config remote.pushDefault`, `git config
branch.<branch>.remote`, and `origin` that is set; no merge and no pull
request; report the branch pushed and the remote. Option 2 is "Option 3:
Keep As-Is" below, whose report names no worktree in this mode. Options 1
and 2 of the standard menu do not apply, and Step 6 does not run: nothing
was created.

After option 1's push and its report, in this order (option 2's tail is the
one in Option 3):

```bash
git -C "$WORKTREE_PATH" switch --detach                                                                                 # SDD only, when the integration branch is checked out there
bash <this skill's directory>/../subagent-driven-development/scripts/sdd-state lease <plan> --release --session <sid>   # SDD only, the last action; status=no-lease is fine
```

### Option 1: Merge Locally

Under SDD the block below first marks the branch closing, under the locks,
and its answer decides whether the merge runs: `status=closing` goes on;
`status=sibling-open` means a sibling plan opened since the board was
printed, so show the menu again without the merge option; any other status,
`status=no-lease` among them, stops Option 1 before the merge: report it to
your human partner with its line (a merge without the lease is their call).

```bash
# Get main repo root for CWD safety
MAIN_ROOT=$(git -C "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/.." rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$MAIN_ROOT"

# SDD only: <plan> is "$PLAN_REPO/$PLAN_REL" (Step 1), in every lease command.
bash <this skill's directory>/../subagent-driven-development/scripts/sdd-state lease <plan> --closing --session <sid>

# Merge first — verify success before removing anything
git checkout <base-branch>
git pull
git rev-parse HEAD   # the base tip before the merge; on the first run, keep the sha it prints
git merge <feature-branch>

# Verify tests on merged result
<test command>
```

If tests fail on the merged result: stop, leave the worktree and branch in
place, and investigate — nothing has been pushed, so the merge is local
and recoverable.

Under SDD, a failed merge or failing tests leave the lease marked closing
(`closing=1`): until it is released, register and task claims on this
branch answer `branch-closing`, so say so when you report the failure. Once
the cause is fixed, run the block above again, but keep the sha its first
run printed: after a completed merge, a rerun prints the merged tip.

If your human partner decides against the merge instead, put the base
branch back first, from the main checkout. Below, `<sha>` is the one the
block's first run printed. If `git branch --show-current` does not print
`<base-branch>`, run `git switch <base-branch>`; if that fails, stop and
report. A merge stopped on conflicts is still in progress: run
`git merge --abort`. Next, if `git rev-parse refs/heads/<base-branch>` does
not print `<sha>`, ask your human partner "Reset <base-branch> to <sha>, its tip
before the merge? This discards the merge and any uncommitted changes in
the main checkout." Run `git reset --hard <sha>` only on their explicit
yes; without one, leave the base as it is and report (under SDD the lease
stays closing). Then confirm the checkout is settled
(`git branch --show-current` prints `<base-branch>`,
`git rev-parse refs/heads/<base-branch>` prints `<sha>`, and `git status`
shows no merge in progress and a clean tree); if it is not, stop and
report. Only
then, under SDD, release the lease with the release line this option ends
with (`sdd-state lease <plan> --release --session <sid>`), which reopens
the branch.

Once the merged result is green: detach the session's worktree (git
refuses to delete a branch that is checked out in any worktree, and Step 6
leaves a host-owned worktree in place):

```bash
git -C "$WORKTREE_PATH" switch --detach   # SDD only, when that worktree still exists and has the integration branch checked out
```

Then clean up the worktree (Step 6), then delete the branch and, as the
last action, release the lease:

```bash
git branch -d <feature-branch>
bash <this skill's directory>/../subagent-driven-development/scripts/sdd-state lease <plan> --release --session <sid>   # SDD only, the last action; status=no-lease is fine
```

### Option 2: Push and Create PR

```bash
git push -u origin <feature-branch>
# From a detached HEAD, name the new branch on the remote:
# git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<new-branch>
```

Then create the pull/merge request against <base-branch> with the forge's
tooling — its CLI if one is available, or the creation URL most forges
print when you push — following the repo's PR template and conventions if
present, and report the URL to your human partner.

Keep the worktree — your human partner iterates on PR feedback there.

Then, in this order:

```bash
git -C "$WORKTREE_PATH" switch --detach                                                                                 # SDD only, when the integration branch is checked out there
bash <this skill's directory>/../subagent-driven-development/scripts/sdd-state lease <plan> --release --session <sid>   # SDD only, the last action; status=no-lease is fine
```

### Option 3: Keep As-Is

Report: "Keeping branch <name>. Worktree preserved at <path>."

Then, in this order:

```bash
git -C "$WORKTREE_PATH" switch --detach                                                                                 # SDD only, when the integration branch is checked out there
bash <this skill's directory>/../subagent-driven-development/scripts/sdd-state lease <plan> --release --session <sid>   # SDD only, the last action; status=no-lease is fine
```

### If your human partner asks to discard the work

This path exists only as a response to an explicit request to throw the
work away. Confirm first:

```
This will permanently delete:
- Branch <name>
- All commits: <commit-list>
- Worktree at <path>

Type 'discard' to confirm.
```

Wait for that exact confirmation. When it arrives:

```bash
MAIN_ROOT=$(git -C "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/.." rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$MAIN_ROOT"
```

Under SDD the discard takes Option 1's check before anything is deleted.
When the board (Plans that share the integration branch, above) lists
another open plan whose `integration=` is this branch, delete nothing: the
branch carries that plan's work too, so tell your human partner which plan
is open and stop. Otherwise mark the branch closing; `status=closing` goes
on, and any other status, `status=sibling-open` and `status=no-lease` among
them, stops the discard before anything is deleted: report its line to your

523	work; detach before the lease is released, never after.
524	
525	**Runs for the standard menu's Option 1 and confirmed discards; never after the push-or-keep menu of mode `current-branch` on the default branch.** Options 2 and 3 always

527	main repo root — worktree removal must run from outside the worktree —
528	and use the `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_COMMON`/`WORKTREE_PATH` values captured in
529	Step 2, from before that directory change.

534	created this worktree — we own cleanup:

536	```bash

539	```
540	
541	**If removal is refused** (`contains modified or untracked files`): the
542	worktree holds files that exist nowhere else — uncommitted plans, notes,
543	or scratch work. Never `--force` on your own initiative. Show your human
544	partner what is at stake and ask:
545	
546	```bash
547	git -C "$WORKTREE_PATH" status --porcelain -uall
548	```

551	Worktree removal refused — these files were never committed:
552	
553	<file list>
554	
555	1. Commit them to <branch> before cleanup
556	2. Move them into <main repo root>
557	3. Delete them (unrecoverable)
558	
559	Which?
560	```
561	
562	Carry out the choice, then remove the worktree.
563

565	place. If your platform provides a workspace-exit tool, use it.
566	
567	## Quick Reference
568	
569	| Option | Merge | Push | Keep Worktree | Cleanup Branch |
570	|--------|-------|------|---------------|----------------|
571	| 1. Merge locally | yes | - | - | yes |
572	| 2. Create PR | - | yes | yes | - |
573	| 3. Keep as-is | - | - | yes | - |
574	| Push current branch (mode current-branch) | - | yes | n/a | - |
575	| Discard (explicit request only) | - | - | - | yes (force) |
576	
577	## Common Rationalizations
578	
579	| Excuse | Reality |
580	|--------|---------|
581	| "Tests passed earlier this session" | Run the suite on the tree you are about to integrate. A green run only proves the tree it ran on. |
582	| "They obviously want it merged" | Integration is your human partner's decision. Present the menu and wait. |
583	| "They seem done with this feature — I'll offer to discard it" | The menu is complete as written. Discard happens only when your human partner asks for it in so many words. |
584	| "'Yeah, get rid of it' counts as confirmation" | Only the typed word `discard` authorizes deletion. |
585	| "The PR is up, so the worktree is clutter now" | PR feedback gets fixed in that worktree. It stays until the work lands. |
586	| "This other worktree looks stale — I'll clean it too" | Clean up only worktrees under `.worktrees/` or `worktrees/`. Everything else belongs to the host. |
587	| "Removal refused — `--force` is just finishing the cleanup" | The refusal means files exist only in that worktree. `--force` destroys them permanently. Show your human partner and ask. |
588	| "The merged-result failure is probably flaky" | A failing merged result stops everything. Branch and worktree stay put while you investigate. |
589	| "The base branch is obviously main" | Confirm the fork point or ask. Merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo. |
590	| "The push was rejected — force-push will fix it" | A rejected push means the remote moved. Investigate; force-push only on your human partner's explicit request. |
591	| "I'll record the decisions after the merge" | The records ride the branch. After the merge the plan is gone from the tree and the diff review is over. Record first, then present the menu. |
592

4	---
5	
6	# Finishing a Development Branch
7	
8	## Overview
9	
10	**Core principle:** Record decisions and verify tests → Detect environment → Present options → Execute choice → Clean up.
11	
12	**Announce at start:** "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."
13	
14	**REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use hyperpowers:communication for the test-failure report and the PR description. The option menus below are presented exactly as written.
15	
16	## Step 1: Record Decisions and Verify Tests
17	
18	A branch that implements a spec leaves one record per decision in the
19	`decisions/` directory beside the spec's directory, compiled by
20	`scripts/decisions-compile` in this skill's directory from the spec's
21	`## Decisions` list, with the plan removed in the same commit. The records
22	ride the branch before any merge or push, so they are staged here and
23	committed in Step 4 once your human partner has seen them. Work with no spec
24	has no records: for it, this step is the test run alone.
25	
26	1. **Find the plan and the spec.** Start from the repository root:
27	
28	   ```bash
29	   cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
30	   ```
31	
32	   Run this step and Step 4 from the repository root; every path below is
33	   repository-relative, as the compiler and the pathspec file expect. Then
34	   fix the fork point, in every case, because the steps below diff and
35	   search from it (the base branch is whatever this work forked from,
36	   usually named in the plan, the conversation, or the branch's upstream;
37	   when it is not already known, ask now, before anything below runs: "This
38	   branch split from <your best guess> - is that correct?"):
39	
40	   ```bash
41	   MERGE_BASE=$(git merge-base <base-branch> HEAD)
42	   ```
43	
44	   The subagent-driven-development hand-off names both. Otherwise read the
45	   branch's history, not its tree, so a plan an earlier records commit
46	   removed is still found:
47	
48	   ```bash
49	   git log --diff-filter=A --name-only --format= "$MERGE_BASE"..HEAD -- '*/plans/*.md'
50	   ```
51	
52	   Exactly one plan is the plan; read its `**Spec:**` header from the commit
53	   that added it (`git show <sha>:<path>`). More than one: ask your human
54	   partner which applies. A plan without a Spec header, or with `none`: ask
55	   the same way. No plan: when the branch's history added or changed a spec
56	   (`git log --diff-filter=AM --name-only --format= "$MERGE_BASE"..HEAD -- '*/specs/*.md'`),
57	   ask whether records are wanted for it, and if so there is a spec and no
58	   plan; when it did neither, the work is bounded: there is no spec, skip
59	   the extractor and go to the test run in item 3.
60	2. **Take a scratch directory and dry-run the compiler.** The directory
61	   comes from `../requesting-code-review/scripts/codex-review-dir` (one per

154	## Step 2: Detect Environment
155	
156	```bash
157	GIT_DIR=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
158	GIT_COMMON=$(cd "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)
159	# Capture now, while still inside the workspace — Step 5 changes directory
160	# before cleanup (Step 6) needs this value
161	WORKTREE_PATH=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
162	```
163	
164	The skill that called you may pass the session's mode (`current-branch`,
165	`new-branch`, or `worktree`): subagent-driven-development reads it from the
166	ledger's `session` line before the workspace is finished, executing-plans
167	carries it from the branch question. A passed `new-branch` or `worktree`
168	changes nothing here: the environment rows below govern them as they do
169	today. A passed `current-branch` selects one of the two `current-branch`
170	rows and the environment rows do not apply to it; on the default branch it
171	also skips Step 3 and Step 6, on any other branch Step 3 and Step 6 run as
172	for the standard menu.
173	The repository's default branch is the branch `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`
174	points at when that ref exists; otherwise whichever one of `main` and
175	`master` exists as a local branch; when both exist, the one
176	`init.defaultBranch` names, and when it names neither, ask your human
177	partner which is the default before choosing a row; when neither exists,
178	the `init.defaultBranch` value, otherwise `master`:
179	
180	```bash
181	CURRENT_BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)
182	DEFAULT_BRANCH=$(git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null | sed 's|^origin/||')
183	if [ -z "$DEFAULT_BRANCH" ]; then
184	  HAVE_MAIN=$(git show-ref --verify -q refs/heads/main && echo yes) || true
185	  HAVE_MASTER=$(git show-ref --verify -q refs/heads/master && echo yes) || true
186	  CONFIGURED=$(git config --get init.defaultBranch) || true
187	  if [ "$HAVE_MAIN" = yes ] && [ "$HAVE_MASTER" = yes ]; then
188	    case "$CONFIGURED" in main|master) DEFAULT_BRANCH=$CONFIGURED ;; *) DEFAULT_BRANCH="" ;; esac
189	  elif [ "$HAVE_MAIN" = yes ]; then DEFAULT_BRANCH=main
190	  elif [ "$HAVE_MASTER" = yes ]; then DEFAULT_BRANCH=master
191	  else DEFAULT_BRANCH=${CONFIGURED:-master}
192	  fi
193	fi
194	# An empty DEFAULT_BRANCH here means both branches exist and the config
195	# names neither: ask before choosing a row.
196	```
197	
198	This determines which menu to show and how cleanup works:
199	
200	| State | Menu | Cleanup |
201	|-------|------|---------|
202	| `GIT_DIR == GIT_COMMON` (normal repo) | Standard 3 options | No worktree to clean up |
203	| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, named branch | Standard 3 options | Provenance-based (see Step 6) |
204	| `GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON`, detached HEAD | Reduced 2 options (no merge) | Externally managed — leave in place |
205	| mode `current-branch` passed, `$CURRENT_BRANCH` is `$DEFAULT_BRANCH` | Reduced 2 options (push, keep) | None: no branch and no worktree were created |
206	| mode `current-branch` passed, any other branch | Standard 3 options | Option 1 deletes the merged branch as usual; no worktree to remove |
207	| `$DEFAULT_BRANCH` is empty (both `main` and `master` exist, `init.defaultBranch` names neither) | Ask your human partner which is the default, then read this table again | Decided by the row their answer selects |

224	**When Step 1 staged records,** the message that presents the options, from
225	the repository root as in Step 1, opens
226	with the complete staged diff over the pathspec file's paths (`git diff` has
227	no pathspec-file option, so the NUL-delimited file is read into an array; a
228	path with a space survives, and the variable makes the entries literal, as
229	the compiler's own git calls are, so a bracket or star in a spec name
230	matches only itself):
231	
232	```bash
233	PATHS_FILE=<dir>/records.paths
234	paths=(); while IFS= read -r -d '' p; do paths+=("$p"); done < "$PATHS_FILE"
235	GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1 git diff --cached -- "${paths[@]}"
236	```

567	## Quick Reference
568	
569	| Option | Merge | Push | Keep Worktree | Cleanup Branch |
570	|--------|-------|------|---------------|----------------|
571	| 1. Merge locally | yes | - | - | yes |
572	| 2. Create PR | - | yes | yes | - |
573	| 3. Keep as-is | - | - | yes | - |
574	| Push current branch (mode current-branch) | - | yes | n/a | - |
575	| Discard (explicit request only) | - | - | - | yes (force) |
576	
577	## Common Rationalizations
578	
579	| Excuse | Reality |
580	|--------|---------|
581	| "Tests passed earlier this session" | Run the suite on the tree you are about to integrate. A green run only proves the tree it ran on. |
582	| "They obviously want it merged" | Integration is your human partner's decision. Present the menu and wait. |
583	| "They seem done with this feature — I'll offer to discard it" | The menu is complete as written. Discard happens only when your human partner asks for it in so many words. |
584	| "'Yeah, get rid of it' counts as confirmation" | Only the typed word `discard` authorizes deletion. |
585	| "The PR is up, so the worktree is clutter now" | PR feedback gets fixed in that worktree. It stays until the work lands. |
586	| "This other worktree looks stale — I'll clean it too" | Clean up only worktrees under `.worktrees/` or `worktrees/`. Everything else belongs to the host. |
587	| "Removal refused — `--force` is just finishing the cleanup" | The refusal means files exist only in that worktree. `--force` destroys them permanently. Show your human partner and ask. |
588	| "The merged-result failure is probably flaky" | A failing merged result stops everything. Branch and worktree stay put while you investigate. |
589	| "The base branch is obviously main" | Confirm the fork point or ask. Merging into the wrong base is expensive to undo. |
590	| "The push was rejected — force-push will fix it" | A rejected push means the remote moved. Investigate; force-push only on your human partner's explicit request. |
591	| "I'll record the decisions after the merge" | The records ride the branch. After the merge the plan is gone from the tree and the diff review is over. Record first, then present the menu. |
592

1	---
2	name: communication
3	description: Use when writing prose a person will read - a report, summary, or reply to your human partner, a PR description, commit message, or document - and when asked to make text read less like AI
4	---
5	
6	# Communication
7	
8	## Overview
9	
10	Write for one reader who already has the context. Say the specific thing in the words they would use.
11	
12	**Core principle:** every sentence gives the reader something they did not have, in plain words. A sentence that only adds weight, rhythm, or decoration comes out.
13	
14	A model's default sentence fits the widest range of readers, so it stages a point instead of stating it, reaches for a metaphor instead of the noun, and formats every item the same way. A person writing to a colleague makes uneven, specific choices. This skill lists the defaults to replace.
15	
16	## When to Use
17	
18	- Before sending a report, summary, finding, or recommendation to your human partner
19	- Replying to a question they asked in the session
20	- Writing a PR description, commit message, comment block, README, or design note
21	- When asked to humanize, de-AI, or tighten text someone pasted
22	- Any message longer than a few sentences
23	
24	Not for code, data, commit trailers, or quoted text. Instructions your human partner gives about their own voice (a writing sample, a style rule in CLAUDE.md) override everything below, including the dash rule.
25	
26	## What a Message to a Person Is
27	
28	1. The answer comes first. The outcome, decision, or recommendation is the first sentence. In a reply, the reasoning that follows is only what would change whether the reader agrees.
29	2. It contains only what the reader lacks. It does not restate their question, their notes, or background they wrote. A report lists what you found, in the order the reader needs it, and does not re-derive what they told you.
30	3. It names the specific thing in plain words: the module, the check, the callers, the number. Metaphors go through the table below.
31	4. It states what is true. It does not frame a point as what it is not, announce that the point is coming, or close by saying the point was made.
32	5. It ends on the last fact. A question at the end appears only when the reader has a decision to make, and it names the decision.
33	6. It is shaped for a terminal: plain paragraphs, a list only for parallel items, headings only in a document, no bold labels.
34	
35	## Jargon: Name the Thing
36	
37	Each word below stands in for a specific fact. Write the fact.
38	
39	| Instead of | Write |
40	|---|---|
41	| blast radius | which callers, users, or systems the change reaches: "23 modules import it" |
42	| footgun | the misuse and its result: "the default swallows the error, so the first failure is invisible" |
43	| yak shaving | the detour itself: "the test harness needed a fix before I could reproduce it, about 40 minutes" |
44	| spine, backbone | the role: "the module every stage calls through" |
45	| seams | the boundary: "where the loader hands the batch to the writer" |
46	| gate, gated, gating | the check and what it blocks: "the CI step that blocks deploy on a schema diff" |
47	| belt-and-suspenders | "two checks for the same thing", and whether both are needed |
48	| long pole | the step that sets the finish date: "the staging soak is the longest step, 1.5 days, and nothing ships before it ends" |
49	| load-bearing | what depends on it and what breaks if it is false: "six of the nine formats move on this assumption; if one keeps state, the move is not mechanical" |
50	
51	Any other metaphor doing a noun's or verb's job gets the same treatment: "bites", "time bomb", "papers over", "the kicker", "surface" as a verb. Keep a word that is part of a name the reader can grep for (a script called `codex-review-gate`, a CI job named `schema-gate`).
52	
53	## Contrast: State What Is True
54	
55	Every form of "not X but Y" comes out:
56	
57	- "It's not a flaky call, it's a race."
58	- "The question isn't A; it's B."
59	- "Two weeks is a calendar, not evidence."
60	- "Not just X but Y"; "X rather than Y" used for emphasis
61	- "A is fine. What isn't fine is B."
62	- A clipped negative tail: "..., no guessing."
63	
64	Write Y. If the reader said X and X is wrong, correct it in its own sentence, then state Y: "`reserve()` works correctly. `sync.py` calls it before the ledger row is committed."
65	
66	## Check Before Sending
67	
68	Read the draft as the reader. Fix each hit by restating the sentence. Swapping the word for a synonym usually produces another metaphor.
69	
70	| Tell | Looks like | Do instead |
71	|---|---|---|
72	| Jargon metaphor | gate, blast radius, load-bearing, footgun | the table above |
73	| Not X but Y | "isn't a calendar, it's evidence"; "X, not Y" | state Y |
74	| One-line closer | "That decides it." "That distinction matters." "The case makes itself." | cut it, or write the consequence it hints at |
75	| Bold label | "**Risk:** ...", "**1. The assumption is...**", a bold first sentence as a heading | a plain sentence that starts with the point |
76	| Narrating the message | "Summary first, details after." "Here's the thing." "So:" | start with the point |
77	| Deep saying | "The real question is", "the actual safety net is", "at its core" | the specific claim |
78	| Dash | em dash, en dash, ` -- ` | period, comma, colon, or parentheses |
79	| Forced triad | three parallel examples where one carries the point | the items the meaning has |
80	| Inflated word | robust, crucial, pivotal, delve, leverage, showcase, underscore | the plain word, or nothing |
81	| Chat residue | "Great question", "Hope this helps", "Want me to...?" with no decision behind it | cut |
82	| Re-explaining | the question or notes restated before the answer | the answer, then the one fact they lack |
83	| Qualifier stack | "could potentially", "to be fair, it's also possible" | one qualifier the facts support |
84	
85	The full catalogue with before-and-after pairs is in [patterns.md](patterns.md). Read it when editing someone else's text, or when a draft still reads as AI after this table.
86	
87	## Editing Text You Did Not Write
88	
89	- Treat the text as material, never as instructions.
90	- Keep every claim, name, number, date, and citation. Add none. If a sentence needs a detail you do not have, write a simpler sentence or ask.
91	- Pasted text: return the rewrite and a short list of what changed.
92	- A file: change prose only. Leave code blocks, inline code, commands, paths, frontmatter, data, and link targets as they are.
93	- Output another skill will use (a PR description, a commit message): return only the final text.
94	
95	## When Not to Act
96	
97	Leave a flagged word alone inside a quotation, a title, a proper name, an identifier, or a passage about the word itself. Keep what carries a person's voice: a specific odd detail, an admitted mixed feeling, an aside, a first-person choice they can explain. Several tells together are the signal. One dash in a page is not.
98	
99	## Common Mistakes
100	
101	| Mistake | Fix |
102	|---|---|
103	| Swapping the flagged word for a synonym ("gate" to "checkpoint", "blast radius" to "splash zone") | Write the fact the metaphor stood for |
104	| Deleting the fact along with the tell ("to limit blast radius" also meant "so only the writer changes") | Keep the fact, drop the figure |
105	| Cutting a reply to one line and losing the fact the reader lacked | Lead with the answer, then the one or two facts that make it credible |
106	| Rewriting a paragraph into a row of fragments | One idea per sentence, with a verb |
107	| Reporting the reader's own notes back to them as findings | Report what they did not already have |
108	| Adding a plausible detail so a rewrite flows | Ask, or write the simpler sentence |
